summary: I take a small number of engagements a year and spend the rest of the time building the tools the engagements keep showing me are missing. Retrieval that cites its sources and build tooling that is honest about its inputs are the two threads.
achievements: Designed and built a permission-aware retrieval platform end to end, from schema through deployment
Published a content-addressed build cache whose key is a hash of a task's declared inputs rather than its branch
Kept two earlier projects maintained rather than abandoned, which is where most of what I know about the first design came from

summary: I work on the layer between product teams and the infrastructure they deploy onto: request limiting, service templates, and the tracing that tells a team whether the slow part is theirs.
achievements: Replaced an exact rate limiter whose failure mode was refusing all traffic with a lease-based one that degrades to a local budget
Wrote the service template that new services start from, including tracing and health checks that work before anyone edits them
Moved the shared counter off the request hot path, which removed limiter latency from three teams' tail latency reports
Ran the review that turned undeclared build inputs from a recurring mystery into a build-time failure
Added a drift metric to the limiter, so an approximate system reports its own error instead of being trusted to have none

summary: Short engagements building internal tools for teams that had outgrown a spreadsheet. Most of the work was deciding what not to build, since every brief arrived described as a general system and every real need was a specific one.
achievements: Built a self-serve reporting console around a fixed query vocabulary instead of the general builder the brief asked for
Delivered an appointment and roster tool that replaced a shared spreadsheet, with an export the previous process depended on
Handed over each project with a written runbook, because a solo engagement with no handover is a liability disguised as a delivery

summary: I maintained the evaluation harness for a retrieval group and ran the comparisons that went into two papers. Most of the job was keeping the question set and the judgements stable enough that a comparison meant something.
achievements: Rebuilt the evaluation harness so a run was reproducible from a commit and a question set rather than from someone's shell history
Documented the judgement criteria that had until then lived in the head of whoever made them

summary: A summer on an internal tools team. I shipped a small feature end to end and spent the rest of the time reading a codebase considerably older than my experience of them.
achievements: Shipped a saved-filters feature, including the migration and its rollback, with a senior engineer reviewing every step

summary: Four years of the fundamentals, with a final-year project on retrieval over a corpus that was too small for the techniques I wanted to use and taught me more for it.
achievements: Final-year project on passage retrieval, which is the thread most of the work since has followed
Teaching assistant for two semesters of introductory programming
